questions.question: Replace "very happy" with a single, more precise word.

points.text: Ecstatic, overjoyed, elated, jubilant, delighted (any of these or similar).

questions.question: What is the difference in connotation between "cheap" and "inexpensive"?

points.text: "Cheap" has negative connotations of poor quality. "Inexpensive" has neutral/positive connotations of good value. Same basic meaning, different emotional impact.

questions.question: Rewrite "She walked slowly across the room" using a powerful verb instead of walked + slowly.

points.text: She crept/ambled/trudged/meandered/strolled across the room (any precise verb that shows slow movement).

questions.question: Why should you avoid using words you don't fully understand?

points.text: Misused ambitious vocabulary is obvious to examiners and loses marks. It shows lack of control. Better to use simpler vocabulary correctly than ambitious vocabulary incorrectly.

questions.question: Give three alternatives to "said" for angry dialogue.

points.text: Snapped, growled, hissed, retorted, barked, snarled (any three of these or similar).
